annotations.text:
A · Sketch grid — the attached sketch, literally.
Two by two at every width, screenshots tilted and broken out of the card top. Reads as a toy shelf.
Tradeoff: at 390px the two-up cards leave ~150px of text width, so the blurbs have to be short — that is the least SEO copy of the three.

B · Marquee row — four abreast, editorial hero.
Left-aligned hero so the h1 and the paragraph read as one block; cards straight-on and equal weight.
Tradeoff: four equal cards say all four tools are equally real. Three of them are not.

C · Featured — the shipped tool leads.
The dex builder gets a split hero card with a real screenshot and a solid CTA; the other three sit in a supporting row.
Tradeoff: it buries the league builder, which is the tool with a settled spec and the next page to rank.

SEO structure, same in all three:
· h1 carries "make your own Pokédex" plus region and league.
· Each card is an <h2> that exactly matches its slug: /custom-pokedex-builder, /pokemon-league-builder, /favorite-pokemon-picker.
· The footer repeats the four links as anchor text.
Watch out: making / a router moves the dex builder off the URL that ranks today (~pos 7.8 for "pokedex builder").

D · Poster cards — built from your PowerPoint.
Each phone is a WHOLE mobile viewport screenshot at its own proportions: nothing is scaled up or cropped, so the right edge and both top corners stay visible. It overhangs the tile on the top and left, stops well short of the right edge, and runs off the BOTTOM — the only edge that cuts it. A red gradient rises from that bottom edge and the copy sits on it, hiding the cut.
The phones are a fanned pair at -4 degrees, offset like a stacked deck. The back one is a second screen from the same tool, not a duplicate.

Why the tiles are wide and short: a phone screenshot is about 1:1.6, so it only outruns the tile's bottom edge while still being narrow enough to leave bare tile on the right. Make the tile TALL and the phone has to be blown up past the tile's own width to reach the bottom — which is exactly what made the last version look clipped on the right.
Three rules now fail the build instead of being caught by eye: the phone must outrun the tile's bottom, it must leave at least 18% of the tile bare on its right, and the grid's top padding must clear the overhang so the first row does not land on the hero.

Red tile, red gradient, white copy — as asked. This is what the tablet and desktop frames use.
At 390 the tiles are half the screen wide, so the phone nearly fills one: the bare strip on its right is about 34px, against roughly half the tile on desktop. The effect is strongest where the tiles are widest.

White tile, white gradient, dark copy. Identical geometry — only the colour changes — so the pair isolates that one choice.
Quieter, and it keeps red as a signal rather than a surface. Cost: the row loses the block of colour that makes the four read as one shelf.

What one viewport costs on SEO: these cards carry about 45 characters of blurb each, against 150 in direction A, and there is no footer link row. The h2 anchor text and the four slugs are intact, which is the part that matters most.
If you want the longer copy back, keep this exact first screen and put a prose block BELOW the fold. Google indexes the rendered DOM whether or not it is above the fold.
